## Story Goal

Deliver a **per-agent performance report** that a manager can use to compare agents fairly, and that individual agents can open on themselves.

Deliver:

1. A new backend endpoint `GET /api/reports/agents` that returns one row per staff agent for a bounded time window, with these numeric fields:
   - `ticketsResolved` — count of tickets where `assignedAgent === agent._id` and terminal-status timestamp falls inside the window (see Backend §1 for exact status semantics).
   - `chatsHandled` — count of conversations where `assignedAgent === agent._id` **and** the agent posted at least one `Message` on that conversation inside the window (i.e. actually replied after escalation, not just been auto-assigned).
   - `avgFirstResponseMinutes` — for tickets created in-window, mean of `(first non-customer Message.createdAt) − (Ticket.createdAt)` in minutes.
   - `avgResolutionMinutes` — for tickets resolved in-window, mean of `(resolved-status timestamp) − (Ticket.createdAt)` in minutes.
   - `csatAverage` — mean numeric rating from `Feedback` rows whose `parent` points at a ticket or conversation this agent was `assignedAgent` on, submitted in-window.
   - `csatResponseCount` — number of `Feedback` rows contributing to the average.
2. **Role scoping inside the handler:** admin / sub-admin holding `reports:agents:view_all` see every agent's row; a plain agent (any authenticated user with `role === "agent"`) sees only their own row, no permission required. Same ownership-plus-role pattern as customer-management Story 04.
3. A new frontend page at `/reports/agents` that renders the rows as a comparable table with a date-range filter, a specific-agent filter (admin only), and per-row reassign action (admin only) that opens the existing `ReassignAgentMenu` for that agent's currently open assigned tickets.
4. Navigation entry in the staff sidebar/mobile nav gated by "authenticated staff" (agent + admin) — admins land on the full table, agents land on the single-row self view.

**Out of scope:** ticket-volume-only report (Story 39), SLA report (Story 40), CSAT-only report (Story 42), configurable dashboards (Story 43). Do **not** add a new "first response timestamp" column to `Ticket` — derive it from `Message` per the intake note.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** there is no per-agent report. Volume by agent can only be inferred by querying tickets and chats separately.
- **New behaviour:** one endpoint / one page shows tickets-resolved and chats-handled **as two distinct columns**, plus response/resolution time and CSAT. Admin can compare and reassign; agent sees just their own row.
- **Chats-handled definition (from AC):** a conversation only counts if the agent **posted at least one message** on it in-window. Auto-assigned but never-responded chats are excluded — this is the whole point of the "actually responded to after escalation" clause.
- **Comparability requirement:** every metric must be scoped by the same window; the API returns the window echo in the payload so the UI can label the table header unambiguously ("Last 30 days: …").

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Add report permission keys

**File:** `backend/src/constants/permissions.ts`

- Add exactly two new keys, matching the surrounding `"resource:action"` style:
  - `"reports:agents:view_all"` — grants oversight (see every agent row). Assign to the admin and sub-admin default sets that already receive other `view_all`-shaped keys next to `tickets:view_all` / `tickets:reassign`.
  - `"reports:agents:view_self"` — trivial self-view key. Assign to the **agent** default set (and admin/subadmin as a superset). Even though the handler falls back to self-scope for any authenticated agent, an explicit key keeps the nav-gating and permission audit honest per the "every route needs a permission" convention.
- Do **not** collapse the two into one umbrella `reports:agents:*` — granular-per-action is the standing convention.
- Update `backend/tests/constants/permissions.test.ts` to assert both keys exist and are on the expected default role sets.

### 2 — Report validation schema

**Create file:** `backend/src/validation/report.schema.ts`

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { dateRangeSchema } from "./common"; // confirm exact export name in common.ts

export const agentPerformanceQuerySchema = z.object({
  from: z.string().datetime().optional(),
  to: z.string().datetime().optional(),
  agentId: z.string().regex(/^[a-f0-9]{24}$/i).optional(), // scoped by handler: admin-only
});

export type AgentPerformanceQuery = z.infer<typeof agentPerformanceQuerySchema>;
```

- Default window when neither `from` nor `to` supplied: **last 30 days**, applied in the service (not the schema) so the response payload can echo the resolved window.
- Reject windows longer than **90 days** in the schema (`.refine`) to keep aggregate queries bounded; error message: `"Report window cannot exceed 90 days"`.

### 3 — Aggregation service

**Create file:** `backend/src/services/agentPerformance.service.ts`

Export one function:

```ts
export async function getAgentPerformance(input: {
  from: Date;
  to: Date;
  agentId?: string;   // when set, only this agent's row (used for self-scope)
}): Promise<{
  window: { from: string; to: string };
  rows: AgentPerformanceRow[];
}>;
```

Shape:

```ts
export interface AgentPerformanceRow {
  agentId: string;
  agentName: string;
  isActive: boolean;
  ticketsResolved: number;
  chatsHandled: number;
  avgFirstResponseMinutes: number | null;   // null when no in-window tickets
  avgResolutionMinutes: number | null;
  csatAverage: number | null;               // 1..5 (or 1..N — match Feedback model)
  csatResponseCount: number;
}
```

Implementation notes:

- **Agent list:** query `User` for `role: "agent"` (do **not** filter on `isActive` — include historical deactivated agents so admins can see who used to carry load, then flag with `isActive: false`). When the caller passed `agentId`, narrow to that one.
- **ticketsResolved:** `Ticket.aggregate([...])` grouped by `assignedAgent` where either `Ticket.resolvedAt` (if the field exists on the model) OR the ticket-history transition into `resolved` falls in `[from, to]`. Confirm which one the schema actually stores by reading `Ticket.ts` end-to-end; do not invent a field name. If both `resolved` and `closed` are terminal, count each ticket **at most once** (use the earlier of the two).
- **chatsHandled:** join `Conversation` (assigned to the agent) with `Message` (`parentType: "conversation"`, `parentId: conversation._id`, `sender` = agent). Group and count distinct conversations where **at least one** in-window agent-authored message exists. Use `Message.distinct` or an `$lookup` — do not scan messages twice.
- **avgFirstResponseMinutes:** for each in-window ticket, find `min(Message.createdAt)` where `parentType === "ticket"`, `parentId === ticket._id`, and the message sender is **not the customer** (agent, admin, or AI-bot — all count as "first response"). Subtract the ticket's `createdAt`, convert to minutes, average per agent. Tickets with zero replies are excluded from the average (not counted as 0).
- **avgResolutionMinutes:** for each in-window resolved ticket, `(resolvedAt − createdAt)` in minutes. Tickets reopened and re-resolved: use the **latest** resolution instant that still falls in-window.
- **csatAverage / csatResponseCount:** aggregate `Feedback` rows whose parent (ticket or conversation) had `assignedAgent === agent` at the moment feedback was submitted. If the current `Feedback` model does not persist `assignedAgent` at submit-time, join back to the parent's current `assignedAgent` — call out this caveat in a JSDoc comment above the function (it will be revisited when Story 42 builds the standalone CSAT report).
- Return `{ window: { from: from.toISOString(), to: to.toISOString() }, rows }` sorted by `agentName` ascending. **Do not** sort by any metric — that is the client's job.

### 4 — Report route

**Create file:** `backend/src/routes/report.routes.ts`

Register on `/api/reports` in `backend/src/app.ts` next to the other feature routers.

```ts
router.get(
  "/agents",
  requireAuth,
  validate(agentPerformanceQuerySchema, "query"),
  async (req, res) => {
    const isSelfScope =
      !(await callerHasPermission(req, "reports:agents:view_all"));
    if (isSelfScope) {
      // Agents may only look at themselves. Ignore any agentId in the query.
      const selfId = req.user!.id;
      const data = await getAgentPerformance({
        from: resolveFrom(req.query.from),
        to: resolveTo(req.query.to),
        agentId: selfId,
      });
      return res.json(data);
    }
    const data = await getAgentPerformance({
      from: resolveFrom(req.query.from),
      to: resolveTo(req.query.to),
      agentId: (req.query.agentId as string | undefined) ?? undefined,
    });
    res.json(data);
  }
);
```

- Non-agent, non-admin roles (i.e. `customer`) must be rejected with **403** before self-scope kicks in. Enforce with an explicit `if (req.user!.role === "customer") return res.status(403).json({...})` at the top — do not rely on the permission gate alone, because `reports:agents:view_self` might accidentally be granted to a customer in the future.
- Mount in `backend/src/app.ts`: `app.use("/api/reports", reportRoutes);`.
- Log an audit entry `action: "report_viewed"` (add to `AuditLog.ts` action enum if not yet present) capturing `{ report: "agents", window, targetAgentId }` so admin views over sensitive team data are traceable.

### 5 — No changes needed to reassignment endpoint

`PATCH /api/tickets/:id` already handles reassignment under `tickets:reassign` (see `backend/src/routes/ticket.routes.ts` around lines 740–800). The frontend affordance calls it directly. **Do not** duplicate the endpoint or add a report-specific reassign route.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty window:** admin picks a date range with zero activity — service returns rows for every agent with all metrics `0` / `null`, and the page renders the empty-metrics dashes. Enforced by the service's per-row default construction.
- **Agent with no CSAT responses:** `csatAverage` is `null`, `csatResponseCount` is `0`. UI shows `"—"` not `"0.0 ★"`.
- **Deactivated agent inside window:** row still shows (with `isActive: false` badge) so historical work is credited. Reassign affordance is **hidden** for inactive agents because they can't take new work.
- **Ticket resolved then reopened then re-resolved in-window:** counted **once** using the latest in-window resolution instant. Enforced in `agentPerformance.service.ts` §3.
- **Chat auto-assigned but agent never replied:** excluded from `chatsHandled`. Enforced by the `$lookup`/distinct message check in §3.
- **Agent posted a private/internal note but never a customer-visible reply:** still counts as `chatsHandled` — the AC says "actually responded", not "responded publicly". Executor should confirm current `Message` model has no internal-vs-external distinction that would change this; if it does, use the public flag and document the choice inline.
- **Non-ASCII agent names (Arabic):** name column must render RTL correctly under the Arabic locale. Matches existing table conventions.
- **Window > 90 days:** rejected at the schema layer with a 400 and the message above. Filter bar disables submit or shows validation error if `to − from > 90d`.
- **`agentId` supplied by a self-scope caller:** silently ignored; response contains only the caller's row. Do **not** 403 — 403 would leak that the queried agent exists.
- **Concurrent reassignment during report view:** the report is a snapshot; the reassign affordance calls `PATCH /api/tickets/:id` which will 409/400 on stale assignments as it already does. The page invalidates its own data (`router.refresh()`) after a successful reassignment.
- **Customer role hits `GET /api/reports/agents` directly:** 403 with `{ error: "Not authorized" }`. Enforced at top of handler in §4.

## Test Plan

1. **Unit — service:** `backend/tests/services/agentPerformance.service.test.ts` (new). Seed 2 agents, mixed tickets (resolved, open, reopened), chats (assigned+replied, assigned+silent), and feedback rows; assert every column matches expected values. Cover the reopened-then-re-resolved case.
2. **Unit — service:** empty window returns rows for all agents with `0` / `null`.
3. **Unit — service:** deactivated agent appears with `isActive: false` and correct historical counts.
4. **Integration — route:** `backend/tests/routes/report.routes.test.ts` (new).
   - `GET /api/reports/agents` as admin — returns all rows.
   - As agent — returns only the caller's row, even if `?agentId=<peer>` was passed.
   - As customer — 403.
   - Window > 90 days — 400 with the guard message.
   - Missing `from`/`to` — defaults to last 30 days; response `window` echo matches.
5. **Integration — permission test:** `backend/tests/constants/permissions.test.ts` — assert `reports:agents:view_all` on admin+subadmin, `reports:agents:view_self` on agent+admin+subadmin, neither on customer.
6. **Frontend smoke:** manual walk-through — an admin loads `/reports/agents`, filters to last 7 days, sees all rows; picks one agent, sees just that row; clicks reassign on a row, hands one open ticket to another online agent, sees the row's `ticketsResolved` unchanged and the ticket queue reflect the new owner.
7. **Frontend smoke:** an agent user loads `/reports/agents`, sees only their own row; the "Reassign" column is absent; the agent-picker filter is absent.
8. **Frontend smoke:** a customer navigates to `/reports/agents` — sees the disabled/greyed nav state (never the page).
